title: A management bridge exposes an operation that takes a URI; the broker fetches it and a bean factory instantiates it
index_line: T-0027 · EXEC · Jolokia exec → addNetworkConnector(URI) → broker fetches remote Spring XML → ProcessBuilder bean · java/any-JMX-bridge · corroborated
invariant_violated: The management plane is assumed to be post-exploitation: if you can call it, you already own the box. But a management operation that accepts a *URI* turns a control-plane call into an outbound fetch, and the fetched document is interpreted by a bean factory — so control-plane access becomes code execution, and the component that should only be configured becomes the execution engine.

mechanism.does: a request reaches the JMX-over-HTTP bridge and names an MBean operation with arguments
the bridge resolves the mbean/operation names against the live MBean server — the default policy allows exec on every application MBean
the chosen operation registers a network connector whose discovery URI carries a broker-config parameter pointing at an attacker-hosted document
the broker resolves that URI and fetches the document, treating an arbitrary resource as its own configuration
the configuration is a Spring bean definition, and the factory instantiates every singleton bean — including ones whose constructor or init-method runs a process
the command runs in the broker's JVM before the broker decides the resulting object was not a usable broker

source.http.body.value: the Jolokia JSON exec body (`mbean`, `operation`, `arguments`) — or any JMX/actuator/admin bridge with an exec-style endpoint

sink.http.request.value: the server-side fetch of the attacker's URI — the SSRF that is not the impact, just the delivery

delegate.tool.value: the bean/config/document factory that instantiates attacker-named classes (Spring `ResourceXmlApplicationContext`, xbean, SpEL, template loaders)

fs.path.join.value: the resource-URI scheme selector: only some schemes can be dereferenced from the config loader, so the scheme is the working part of the payload

guard.none.value: the bridge's access policy permits exec on all application MBeans; there is no operation allow-list

preconditions.expr: the JMX/HTTP bridge is exposed and its access policy permits exec on application MBeans

check.spec: curl -s -u admin:admin http://HOST:8161/api/jolokia/version | head -c 200; curl -s -u admin:admin 'http://HOST:8161/api/jolokia/exec/org.apache.activemq:type=Broker,brokerName=localhost/addNetworkConnector(java.lang.String)/x' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'

preconditions.expr: an operation exists whose argument is a URI the server will dereference
default or weak console credentials, or the bridge is reachable without auth (the vendor's own default is a well-known admin pair)
build is inside the affected range (ActiveMQ < 5.19.4 or 6.0.0–6.2.2)

success: the exec call returns status 200 with a non-null value, and the broker log then shows the attacker URI in an 'Establishing network connection' line
the broker fetches the attacker's XML (visible in the attacker's HTTP log) and a child process appears under the broker JVM
the command repeats on the connector's retry timer — one request, many executions
failure_like: the bridge answers 403/404 for exec, or the policy denies the MBean — nothing to drive
no operation in the MBean takes a dereferenceable URI
false_positive: a 200 from a different Jolokia operation (e.g. `version`) — proves the bridge is up, not that exec is permitted
a broker-log warning that the connector could not connect: that message is *after* the fact, the bean already ran — do not read it as failure
attributing execution to the access log; the evidence is in the broker log and in child processes

hazards: the honest CVSS for this one is PR:L (an authenticated console user); it is KEV'd because default console credentials are the norm, so establish credentials before claiming pre-auth
the retry timer means a single request produces repeated fetches — clean up the connector or the lab keeps calling you
management planes are systematically under-audited: Actuator, Jolokia, JMX, admin RPC, and debug endpoints all take operations whose arguments reach file/URL loaders
the vendor's first patch was bypassed (CVE-2026-42588) — check the target build against the current advisory, not the first fixed release
non_transfers: bridges whose access policy is a strict operation allow-list rather than a per-MBean exec flag
config loaders that refuse non-local resource schemes (the fix: the broker no longer loads brokerConfig over an arbitrary URI)
